verdict.rationale: Sill's public GitHub repository includes build-from-source instructions: SwiftPM builds of Sill.app, running SillHost from the command line, and changing the bundle identifier for your own signing. That shows the source is publicly readable. Nothing in the pack names a license, so the open-license half of the story is unevidenced. Missing for 10: an explicit open-source license (e.g. MIT/Apache/GPL) for the repository, and independent confirmation of the licensing terms.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: This builds Sill.app with SwiftPM, signs it with your Apple Development identity, replaces /Applications/Sill.app and opens it.
`swift run -c release SillHost` runs the same host on the command line
In the Sill target's Signing & Capabilities, pick your team, and change the bundle identifier `me.saffer.sill` to one of your own.
